title: Lab 7 — Quiz 1
subtitle: Bacterial Genetics — DNA structure and replication

questions.prompt: Which enzyme unzips the DNA double helix during replication?
questions.explanation: Helicase breaks the hydrogen bonds between bases, creating a replication fork.

why.B: Primase lays down an RNA primer.

questions.prompt: What bond does helicase break when it unzips DNA?

options.text: Covalent bonds between sugar and phosphate
Ionic bonds between the two backbones

questions.explanation: Base pairs are held together by hydrogen bonds; helicase breaks them.

why.A: Those form the backbone; they stay intact.
why.D: The strands are held by hydrogen bonds between bases.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme lays down an RNA primer to direct DNA polymerase?
questions.explanation: Primase lays an RNA primer that directs DNA polymerase where to begin.

why.D: RNA polymerase makes mRNA during transcription.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme forms covalent bonds to join Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand?
questions.explanation: Ligase catalyzes covalent bonds to join the Okazaki fragments.

why.D: Gyrase isn't the enzyme that joins fragments.

questions.prompt: The short fragments made on the lagging daughter strand are called:
questions.explanation: The lagging strand is made in pieces (Okazaki fragments) because DNA polymerase must be removed and re-attached repeatedly.

why.B: Primers start each fragment; they aren't the fragments themselves.
why.D: Promoters signal the start of a gene.

questions.prompt: DNA replication is 'semi-conservative.' This means each daughter molecule has:

options.text: One original strand and one newly made strand
A mix of DNA and RNA nucleotides

questions.explanation: Each daughter molecule consists of one original (template) strand and one newly synthesized strand.

why.B: Each daughter keeps one original strand.
why.D: Daughter DNA is all DNA once the primers are replaced.

questions.prompt: What are the DNA base-pairing rules?

options.text: A pairs with T; G pairs with C
A pairs with U; G pairs with C
A pairs with G; T pairs with C
A pairs with C; G pairs with T

questions.explanation: DNA: A–T and G–C. Each strand serves as a template for a new strand.

why.B: U is found in RNA, not DNA.
why.C: A–T and G–C are the pairs.
why.D: A–T and G–C are the pairs.

questions.prompt: What type of bond links nucleotides along a single strand of DNA?

options.text: Covalent bonds between sugar and phosphate

questions.explanation: DNA polymerase forms covalent bonds between the sugar and phosphate of nucleotides on the growing daughter strand.

why.B: Hydrogen bonds hold the two strands together.
why.D: Disulfide bonds are found in some proteins.

questions.prompt: Which nitrogenous bases are found in RNA?
questions.explanation: DNA: A, T, G, C. RNA: A, U, G, C.

why.B: T is a DNA base; RNA uses U instead.
why.C: RNA has no T; it has A, U, G and C.
why.D: DNA and RNA each use four bases.

questions.prompt: The site on DNA where replication begins is called the:
questions.explanation: Replication begins at an origin of replication, forming a replication fork.

why.A: The promoter is where RNA polymerase binds for transcription.
why.C: The operator is the repressor binding site in an operon.

questions.prompt: Why is the leading strand made continuously while the lagging strand is made in fragments?

options.text: DNA polymerase can only build in one direction, so one strand must be made in pieces
The lagging strand template has no complementary bases
Ligase only works on the leading strand of the DNA
Helicase unzips the lagging strand last of all

questions.explanation: DNA polymerase synthesizes in one direction. On the leading strand it follows helicase continuously; on the lagging strand it must be removed and re-attached, making Okazaki fragments.

why.D: Both strands unzip together at the fork.

questions.prompt: Which end of a nucleotide strand is the 3' end?

options.text: The end with the free phosphate
The end with the free OH on the sugar
The end with the nitrogenous base
Either end, depending on the base

why.A: The free phosphate marks the 5' end.
why.C: Bases stick out from the side of every nucleotide.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme in the replication model adds new nucleotides to synthesize the complementary daughter strands?
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase brings in free nucleotides that hydrogen-bond to the template and forms covalent bonds between them.

why.A: RNA polymerase builds mRNA in transcription.
why.C: Primase only lays down short RNA primers.
why.D: Helicase only unzips the double helix.

questions.prompt: Where does DNA replication occur in a prokaryote?
questions.explanation: Replication happens in the eukaryotic nucleus, or in the cytoplasm of a prokaryote.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the DNA replication model activity is FALSE?

options.text: Helicase unzips the DNA as the molecule is fed through
The lagging strand is made in fragments
The two finished molecules should be identical
The DNA polymerase on the leading strand must be removed and reattached

questions.explanation: It is the LAGGING strand's DNA polymerase that must be removed and reattached for each fragment.
